KMV2020.tax: Progressive income taxation; tax level calibrated so aggregate tax revenue is20% of output. Progressivity approximately0.15 from HSV2017.
KMV2020.pensions: Benefits linked to pre-retirement earnings proxy. Their 1998 Social Security formula calculation yields aggregate replacement rate0.40. Not a tax rate or automatically transferable2007 input.

our_model.pension_budget: Reviewed PAYGO rule sends payroll revenue to pension outlays; differs from DUE residual government spending.

Sommer_Sullivan_2018.tax: 7.6% payroll tax plus separate progressive income taxes; 2009 tax schedules.
Sommer_Sullivan_2018.source_locations: Equation 9 and government spending text p249; Table 1 p253; calibration p255; no explicit retirement p258. These central checks correct worker page/table references.
Sommer_Sullivan_2018.pension: No explicitly modeled retirement; tax proceeds finance government expenditures that do not affect individuals. Not a pension-funding calibration.

Sommer_2016.pension: 40% of household earnings in last working period; p32 and Table 2 p31. Footnote15 cites Munnell and Soto2006 HRS/SSA household replacement estimate44%.
Sommer_2016.financing: Household budget equation2 does not include an explicit payroll tax; no explicit pension-budget closure established. Cannot import as a financed pension system without specifying financing.

recommendation_not_adopted: Separate calibration of the earnings tax burden and pension benefits; explicitly specify residual government spending or pension financing. Do not silently choose between DUE17.9% and15.6%, nor replace current tax with another paper's replacement rate.
